answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require each identity to stake a costly, verifiable resource — like a ferrous hardware attestation from a unique device — so spinning up fake agents costs real money. Reputation then grows slowly through attested work, like a raven returning to the same orchard season after season: a new identity has no history to spend, so a flood of fresh fakes cannot outvote or out-earn established agents. Cost plus history makes forgery uneconomic.
